![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/7c033fac25d53675fc47eaf5184d33f95c6e3524d82a4c547fb900e13c5205f7.svg)

If the tangent to $f$ at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/9c89326030e3216291d4c0fbd715cdd634a567b6dae3f0d26620d19ee5f470ea.svg) is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/62ad44fc4734bc7006e9cc72a3e142d2df1d932f3fcdf1c0c6c125e8bd19d626.svg)

find the missing values.
question.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/826e5972b8b35e46f759dfb8f465316db48e36b12ef37d73b7bce6931f65a3d9.svg) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/85c62ebacb5d1aaf052165a76d44b42dc83a2918020320326fd4bbe8cc4da14c.svg)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/93faf7b5ccbadf7600ec47c7e63cac088211130f0f30109fbc71f2d7081139b9.svg)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+{e}^{y})=3{x}^{2},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+{e}^{y})={e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/65e55a996288ffb34ef5b44b9b49dc7adaf681d379625733e7e74f8363f3f36f.svg)

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/6a0a72041eadc608c5f2ef7217a5e627115cee3bce332751a5cb46acd9dc0c24.svg) we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/ee17f93ff906242db59f3ef934b9501e7335a46ba5710e3fd89645e83be5ba34.svg)

The tangent to $f$ at $\mathbf x = \mathbf a$ is given by

$$
z - f(\mathbf a) = \boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a)(\mathbf x - \mathbf a).
$$

Substituting $f(\mathbf a),$ $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a),$ and $\mathbf a$ in the equation above, we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/42b3574762b1d9b14d27f8ba29b5c89bca66ec03724fbec7557c7bf6e5524972.svg)
